candidate_relations.reason: The candidate correctly captures the hemorrhagic stroke in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and lateral ventricle, which is the ipsilateral hemisphere component of the reference diagnosis. However, the reference diagnosis specifically requires the composite of ipsilateral hemisphere hemorrhagic stroke WITH peripheral-type facial paralysis — the unusual finding that the corticobulbar tract thinning on the left (ipsilateral to the lesion) explains a peripheral-pattern facial palsy on the right (ipsilateral to the facial signs), rather than the expected contralateral central-type. This peripheral-type facial paralysis component is entirely absent from the candidate.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the hemorrhagic stroke with precise anatomical localization but omits the defining 'peripheral-type facial paralysis' component that makes this case diagnostically distinctive

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis describes a rare phenomenon: ipsilateral peripheral-type facial palsy from corticobulbar tract involvement ipsilateral to a hemispheric hemorrhage, supported by DTI showing left corticobulbar tract thinning
Candidate omits the key diagnostic novelty (peripheral-type facial paralysis) that distinguishes this from a routine hemorrhagic stroke presentation
